text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United States has urged Albania to pass a constitution and hold parliamentary elections after local ballots on October 20.

- Leaders of Albania's ethnic Greek community have complained to U.S. ambassador Marisa Lino over the closure of seven Greek language schools since 1993. They said the opening of three schools in regional centres was not enough.

- A batch of 3.5 million polio vaccines has arrived in Albania. The vaccines will be used to fight an outbreak of the disease that has killed 12 people. About two million people will receive vaccinations over two weeks from Monday.
- The oppositon Socialist Party has rehabilitated two vice chairmen who opposed a motion for change by their jailed leader Fatos Nano.
- The ruling Democratic Party has infringed election law by putting up posters of its candidate for Tirana mayor in schools.
- Coca Cola Tirana Bottling Enterprise says pirate production of the drink has reduced its share of the Albanian market to only 20 percent.

- About 200,000 people will strike in the transport, education, health and telecommunications sectors today after trade unions and the government failed to reach an agreement on compensation for rising bread and fuel prices.
- Albania's Confederation of Trade Unions says it will stage protest meetings after today's 24-hour strike.
- Private television stations and radios in Albania are in a difficult position because they are neither permitted nor prohibited by law.
- Albania's branch of the Helsinki Human Rights committee and opposition parties have protested at a decision by the central election commission that election monitors must be over the age of 25.
- The Council of Europe has accepted Albanian conditions to retain a law barring former communists from holding public office for five more years.
- Justice Minister Kristofor Peci says corruption is a virus that has infected the courts.

- Germany's parliamentary secretary at the ministry of economic cooperation told Albanian President Sali Berisha that German President Helmut Kohl considers him a friend and supports Berisha and his government.
- Albania and Germany started their first ever military exercises.
